author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Massachusetts State Police trooper accused of punching another off-duty trooper at a Quincy bar appeared in court Thursday, but his arraignment on an assault-and-battery charge was deferred until October 10.

Christopher Regan, 40, is accused of striking the other trooper at The Reel House in June. According to the source report, surveillance video from the bar captured the alleged punch. The other trooper declined to provide investigators with details about the encounter or information about hospital treatment.

State Police said Regan has been relieved of duty while the department prepares a formal hearing on his employment status. The administrative process is separate from the criminal case, which remains pending.

The charge is an allegation, and Regan is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The delayed arraignment means the court has not yet taken the next formal step on the accusation. Additional details about what preceded the encounter, any defense response and the department’s duty-status decision had not been announced in the report.
dek: Christopher Regan is accused of punching another off-duty trooper at a Quincy bar; the charge remains an allegation and the case has not been decided.
headline: Massachusetts trooper’s Quincy assault arraignment deferred to October
